description: "Use when something behaves wrongly and you do not yet know why."

<!-- Generated by Pixl from the skill "Debug with a method", version 1. Edit it in the Skills tab, not here: changes made here are overwritten. -->

## Steps
1. Reproduce it with one command. Write down the exact error or wrong output.
2. Shrink it: find the smallest input that still fails.
3. Locate it: read the code on the path from input to error. Temporary prints are allowed.
4. Write one guess in one line. Test it by looking at values, not by editing.
5. Write a test that fails because of this bug.
6. Fix the cause, not the symptom.
7. Run the new test, then the whole suite. Remove the prints.
## Checklist
- [ ] You can reproduce it with one command.
- [ ] A new test failed before the fix and passes after.
- [ ] The whole suite passes and no print is left.
## Definition of done
The new regression test fails on the old code, passes on the new code, and the suite is green.
## Verify
Run the reproduce command again, then the test command.
## Common mistakes
- Fixing before reproducing.
- Changing several things at once: you cannot tell which one worked.
- Catching the error and hiding it.
- Leaving debug prints in the code.
## Example
Symptom: total shows 100 for an order of 100. Shrunk: `total([100])`. Guess: the check is `>`, not `>=`. Test: `assert total([100]) == 90` fails. Fix the operator. All pass.
